language: zh (with an embedded English clip of Jordi Visser)

mustKnow.item: BTC rose from about 58-64k to about 84-84.5k after the creator's earlier Visser video (roughly +40%, per the creator's own rough estimate)
mustKnow.note: Ours repeats the ASR's 'Joe Dispenza' (0s) as fact. It is almost certainly a mis-hearing of Jordi Visser, the video's subject.

mustKnow.item: Visser's profile (ex-Morgan Stanley, spans Wall Street, AI and crypto): former colleagues running $50-100B+ are asking how to 'play' crypto and tokenization. Wall Street is FOMO-ing late, after retail

Bottom signal: BTC did not fall on bad news (rate hikes, falling odds for the CLARITY Act and its eventual failure, a cold-wallet incident). A small positive (Trump: don't fall behind China, possibly legitimize Hyperliquid) sent it from 64k to 75k and then 84.5k
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge has no levels and no Trump or Hyperliquid catalyst. Ours drops the Hyperliquid-legalization point.

mustKnow.item: Macro: the Fed hiked and the dot plot implies another +25bp this year; BTC still didn't fall
Flows: Wall Street missed Micron and semis. Pomp's scenario has allocations moving from 1% test positions to $10-20B+
Why institutions come: fewer stocks are rising; Nasdaq has outperformed small caps since the iPhone; AI disruption (a Kodak analogy); diversified funds are stuck in laggard stocks
mustKnow.note: Neither has Kodak or the point about diversified funds holding laggards. LeapEdge's 'struggle to outperform the S&P 500' is an inference.

mustKnow.item: 2021-22 crypto was crypto's dot-com bubble; it left rails (L1, L2, Hyperliquid). AI agents are the 'iPhone moment' that will use them, so ETH, BTC, SOL and HYPE rise
Privacy: agents that want confidentiality choose ZEC, which 'rose 10x+'

Actionable conclusion (Peter Lynch): Wall Street doesn't cover individual tokens, and Visser expects broad institutional coverage beyond BTC and ETH around 2027. The retail edge is to research ZEC, SOL and Hyperliquid before 2027
mustKnow.note: Ours states it in k6 and the brief but raises no call. LeapEdge raises calls but upgrades 'research' to 'accumulate' and uses the ticker 'macro'.

ours.text: k8: 'following earlier commentary on Joe Dispenza'
ours.problem: ASR artifact repeated as fact. The context (the title and 24s on) is Jordi Visser. It should be flagged as likely mis-transcription, not asserted.
The name is misspelled; the title has 'Jordi Vissel' and the transcript 'Jordi Visser'.
Loses the proper noun, the CLARITY Act, so a PM can't look it up.

ours.text: keyPoints stance all 'neutral' while tickerSentiment marks everything bullish
ours.problem: Inconsistent. The video is uniformly bullish on crypto.

leapedge.text: tradeIdea ticker 'macro', long, HIGH, 'accumulating leading crypto infrastructure rails'
leapedge.problem: No instrument. The creator's instruction is to research (研究清楚) specific tokens before 2027, not to accumulate. Conviction HIGH is not stated.
This is an illustrative mechanism (agents choose privacy coins, 'ZEC不就起来了吗'), not a recommendation. The better stance is watch or research.

leapedge.text: ZEC quote in English: 'So we go to privacy coins, we go to ZEC. And then ZEC takes off.'
leapedge.problem: The creator's paraphrase is in Chinese. Presenting a back-translation as a verbatim English quote fabricates a quote.

leapedge.text: macro quote: 'Wall Street doesn't cover tokens in crypto, they're starting to get involved in the rails, but they don't cover individual tokens.'
leapedge.problem: The transcript breaks off at 'Wall Street doesn't cover'. The rest cannot be verified from the source.

leapedge.text: 'as they struggle to outperform the S&P 500 index'
leapedge.problem: An inference. The source says diversified funds hold laggard stocks and does not mention an S&P 500 benchmark.

oursMissed: Watch/research ZEC, SOL and Hyperliquid (HYPE) before 2027 institutional coverage (the creator's explicit closing takeaway, 771s-801s). It should be a 'watch' call with horizon 'before 2027'. Ours has ZEC as 'watch' only in tickerSentiment.
leapedgeMissed: SOL and Hyperliquid are named explicitly as research targets but are folded into 'macro'.
leapedgeFalse: 'macro' long HIGH: no instrument, and the action is upgraded from research to accumulation.
ZEC long 'hold or accumulate': the source supports watch/research, not long.

ZEC -> ZEC (spoken as a ticker yet still null)

sentimentIssues: 15 rows for 7 assets: 比特币 x4 plus 'Bitcoin' x1, Ethereum x2 plus ETH x1, Solana x2, Hyperliquid x2. Chinese and English aliases are not merged.
ZEC is spoken literally as 'ZEC' yet has ticker null, which shows the resolver is not even taking tickers spoken outright.
'加密' (crypto, the asset class) is listed as a ticker row.
Stances are inconsistent: sentiment is bullish while stance is 'neutral' for most crypto rows, and Hyperliquid is bullish at 666s but neutral at 745s.
Direction is right: the whole video is bullish on crypto.
why: Ours is more faithful and keeps the levels (58-64k, 75k, 84.5k), flows ($10-20B) and catalysts, but it raises zero calls on a video that ends with a clear directive (research ZEC, SOL and HYPE before 2027). It is too strict here. LeapEdge surfaces the idea but distorts it: the ticker is 'macro', 'research' becomes 'accumulate', conviction is HIGH, and it shows a fabricated English quote. Neither is investment-grade on the call. Ours would win clearly with a watch call and resolved tickers.
recommendations: Let 'watch' and 'research' directives with a horizon become calls. The extraction prompt says to extract 'watch' stances, but critique rejects or drops them when there is no buy verb. Add an explicit rule: 'A creator directive to research, monitor or position before a dated catalyst (e.g. before 2027 institutional coverage) is a watch call with that horizon.'
Take tickers spoken outright (ZEC, ETH, BTC) and resolve crypto names (比特币→BTC, 以太坊/Ethereum→ETH, Solana→SOL, Hyperliquid→HYPE) with a crypto alias table. None needs model inference.
Detect likely ASR name errors ('Joe Dispenza' in a Jordi Visser video) by checking names against the title and channel metadata. Flag them in omissions instead of asserting them.
Merge sentiment rows across Chinese and English aliases (比特币 = Bitcoin = BTC) and across scripts, and drop asset-class rows such as '加密'.
Keep proper nouns for legislation (CLARITY Act) and people (Pomp, Peter Lynch) in keyPoints.
